cohort: The study included US maternal-infant dyads from 2016-2022 whose data was collected through the CDC Pregnancy Risk Assessment Monitoring System (PRAMS).
finding: Perinatal health disparities among Non-Hispanic Black and Hispanic mothers persisted but were not exacerbated during the COVID-19 pandemic (2020-2022) compared to the pre-COVID period (2016-2019), although births during COVID showed a higher prevalence of older mothers with diabetes and hypertension, and Hispanic infants had lower odds of low birthweight during COVID.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was evaluated as a perinatal health outcome.
cross-section timing: Data was collected from 2016-2022, categorized into pre-COVID (2016-2019) and COVID (2020-2022) periods.
